A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JustHook for referring multi-object tracking. Their complete main texts, supplementary sections, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original JustHook benchmark results, component ablations, timing measurements, encoder and tracker analyses, and qualitative examples, including Refer-Dance results in Appendix E.1.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and analyses, including new neighboring-grid, long-range enhancement, and controlled Hook/PCD ablations, alongside retained supplementary results.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming VFH to Hook, v3 introduces trajectory fragmentation, localization noise, and grid recombination to simulate tracking errors. It adds optional text-conditioned long-range reference-point sampling and incorporates the resulting features into PCD. The loss is now described as Focal Loss rather than v2's explicitly entropy-weighted objective, although no replacement formula is provided.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Refer-KITTI, Refer-KITTI-V2, Refer-Dance, and pure tracking on KITTI. Refer-Dance moves from v2 Appendix E.1 to v3's main experiments; it is not new coverage. The added training perturbations do not introduce a separate evaluated domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 drops EchoTrack, DeepSORT, and FairMOT from the Refer-KITTI comparison; FairMOT remains on Refer-KITTI-V2. The principal TransRMOT, TempRMOT, and iKUN comparisons remain. Sequential-decoder alternatives disappear, while an Avg-Pool comparator is added to the OME ablation. Newly discussed LaMOTer is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The reported expression sample count changes from 8 per target to 36, and training introduces four-of-eight frame sampling and tracking-error perturbations. The encoder configurations are substantially revised: BERT and ordinary Swin combinations disappear, while CLIP is added across the supplementary tracker combinations. New Hook/PCD controls disable OME and long-range enhancement. FPS is additionally reported; the principal accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Tables 4–6 add a temporal-pooling control, isolate Hook and PCD under a CLIP configuration, and test neighboring-grid augmentation and long-range reference-point counts across backbones. v2's sequential-decoder comparison and loss-parameter sensitivity study are removed. Freezing, backbone-size, tracker, dataset-correction, and qualitative analyses are retained, although several quantitative results change.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The Gaussian standard deviation introduced in v3 specifies training perturbations, not uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes best-model HOTA from 53.83 to 53.91 on Refer-KITTI and from 42.81 to 41.94 on Refer-KITTI-V2. Reported JustHook inference time changes from 27 minutes to 69 minutes. Freezing, scaling, and tracker-combination scores are extensively revised, and new ablation results replace removed entries. These accompany method and setting changes, so they are not controlled version-to-version performance comparisons. Refer-Dance results, including 31.83 HOTA, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2's explicit entropy-weighted loss definition and detached hard-sample weighting in Equations 3–4 are removed, leaving a brief Focal Loss statement. The bilinear interpolation remains mathematically equivalent. v3's task-relation notation largely reformulates the existing task; its new information-flow discussion introduces no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v3 elevates systematic analysis of tracking/referring interactions to a principal contribution and claims first identification of grid sampling's suitability for RMOT. v2 primarily claims efficient feature extraction and combined-space decoding. Flexible-encoder, accuracy, and efficiency claims remain, while the headline Refer-KITTI-V2 HOTA advantage changes from 7.77 to 6.9 percentage points.

C2.justification: v3 adds information-sufficiency and redundancy arguments, a ground-truth-versus-predicted-trajectory explanation for augmentation, and a distance-based rationale for long-range sampling. It qualifies long-range benefits by backbone and revises the freezing interpretation to distinguish CLIP alignment disruption from RoBERTa domain shift. The earlier limitations concerning dataset complexity, diversity, and scaling are retained.

D1.justification: v3 specifies new implementation parameters, including four-of-eight frame sampling, 0.02% localization-noise standard deviation, 1% recombination, and ten reference points. It omits v2's explicit positive/negative sampling balance, custom-loss parameter choices, and Refer-Dance statement identifying official iKUN detector/tracker outputs. Both PDFs still promise future code availability.

R1.justification: The positioning expands from one-stage versus two-stage RMOT to one-stage RBT, two-stage RBT, and Tracking-by-Referring, incorporating LaMOTer and GroundingDINO. v3 relates grid sampling to ROI pooling and Deformable Attention and frames novelty around subtask information transfer. References also add recent vision-language tracking work and remove several earlier citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem formulation, and method narrative are substantially rewritten around subtask interactions. VFH becomes Hook, OME receives a separate subsection, and RBT/TBR terminology is introduced. Supplementary sections are reordered, Refer-Dance moves into the main experiments, and references move after the supplementary discussion.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout, with extensively redrawn framework and decoder diagrams. v3 adds paradigm and long-range-enhancement figures and removes the dedicated bilinear-sampling illustration. Benchmark tables are condensed, and the timing table adds detection-time and FPS columns. The retained qualitative panels are enlarged and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 Tables 4–6 better support component claims through a pooling control, controlled Hook/PCD comparisons, and evidence that long-range enhancement can hurt Transformer backbones. These provide a limited improvement in experimental support and applicability guidance. The gain is tempered by narrower encoder/decoder comparisons and omitted sampling-balance and Refer-Dance proposal details; the revised headline scores alone do not establish improvement.
